skills.title: What I work with
work.bkd: A customs platform for a private logistics client that handles GB–NI movements end to end through the API of HMRC's Trader Support Service (TSS): safety and security filings (ENS), simplified frontier and supplementary declarations, and full frontier declarations. Data comes in three ways (shipment emails read through Microsoft Graph, Excel uploads or manual entry in the portal) and is extracted, validated and pre-filled, so the team only reviews. Flask on Azure SQL, deployed with Docker.
work.flow.title: Customs Operations Platform
work.gym: A monthly training plan, daily weight log and progress view. Small, fast and exactly as opinionated as I am about leg day.
work.intro: A mix of client work I can talk about and things I built for myself because I wanted them to exist.
work.planning: My own planner: daily focus, a weekly view, an Eisenhower matrix and a vault for decisions. Built because every to-do app I tried was either too much or too little.
work.radar: A GitHub Action wakes up every morning, reads official AI and dev-tooling feeds, and commits a JSON file. This page renders it. The bot touches data, never the layout.
work.site: React and TypeScript with SCSS, built with Vite and prerendered so it reads without JavaScript. Ten languages, light and dark themes, eight accent colours, and built automatically by GitHub Actions on every push.

work.sync.p3: Jobs that fill missing Snowflake data straight from the SAP S/4HANA API, with report generation.
work.sync.p4: File search through SMTP logs and interface movements.
work.sync.p5: In-house AI assistant (beta): built for the company, runs without paid API tokens and resolves administrative support questions.
